text.p: Brazilian steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional's (CSN) chief Sylvio Coutinho resigned on Tuesday, a company spokesman said.
"Sylvio Coutinho submited his resignation letter today and it was accepted by the Board of Directors," the spokesman said.
The board accepted Coutinho's resignation after a day-long meeting in Sao Paulo, he added.

Coutinho, whose official title was changed to director-superintendent for Steel after a company restructuring last May, is to be replaced on an interim basis by Arivair Guido Dall'Stella, director-superintendent for Energy and Infra-structure.
"Dall'Stella will take over Coutinho's duties for about 15 days," the spokesman said.
The company spokesman denied that Coutinho resigned because of disagreements with a possible company lay-off plan.
"Coutinho said his departure has nothing to do with the firm's restructuring process which might involve staff cuts," he said.
Market rumors earlier said Coutinho disagreed with a plan to sack some 2,000 workers. The company has about 13,700 employees.

Coutinho had been CSN chief since the company was privatized in April 1993. The company's main shareholders are Brazil's Vicunha Group, the CSN workforce and pension fund, Banco do Brasil's pension fund and state mining giant Vale do Rio Doce.
